newsitem.title: USA: Coffee shortage sends prices to 34-month high.
newsitem.headline: Coffee shortage sends prices to 34-month high.

text.p: Coffee prices soared to their highest level since July 1994 on Tuesday as continued worries about tight supplies sent speculators on a buying spree.

"It has been a bull market for some time, and the fundamentals remain the same," said Arthur Stevenson, a Prudential Securities analyst. "They include low stocks here in the U.S., a question mark hanging over Colombian production and export capacity, and the well-sold positions of other producers such as Costa Rica."
Dealers said long-term weather outlooks calling for a cool air mass to push across Argentina and into Brazil in 8 to 10 days contributed to today's bullish tone.
However, forecasters said the chance of damaging frost was extremely slim, with the earliest deep freeze in Brazil recorded on May 30-31.
"There is little or no opportunity to produce damaging cold," said Mike Palmerino, Weather Services Corp. senior meterologist. "It's too early, and so far out it's not valid."

But with inventories near 20-year lows, traders said any sign of cool weather in top-grower Brazil was likely to spark buying. Two severe frosts in 1994, one in late June and another in early July, cut Brazil's 1995/96 crop by some 50 percent and sent futures prices to near 10-year highs.
"It's the first time we're seeing cold weather mentioned," said one trader. "And it's a wake-up call."
At New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, arabica coffee for July delivery rose to a lifetime high of 243.00 cents a lb before slipping back slightly to close at 241.15 cents, up 11.50 cents.
Gasoline settled higher in New York after a blast at a Citgo refinery in Texas disrupted production.
A fire after the blast Monday night at the Corpus Christi refinery occurred in the alkylation unit and has shut that and other units at the plant, a spokesman for the company said.

The refinery has capacity to process 132,500 barrels per day of crude oil, while the damaged alkylation unit has a capacity of 21,000 barrels per day. The unit produces high quality gasoline components for premium or cleaner-burning reformulated gasoline.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, June crude settled off one cent a barrel at $21.37. June heating oil was off 0.17 cent a gallon at 56.48 cents, while June gasoline was up 0.29 cent a gallon at 64.76 cents.

Rice futures on the Chicago Board of Trade posted sharp gains for the second straight day, as concern about tight supplies was heightened by reports of Costa Rican buying of rice that is likely to come from the United States.
"The Costa Rica deal is for prompt shipment and they have indicated U.S. origin," a floor source said, referring to news Costa Rica bought 26,500 tonnes for June 30-July 7 shipment.
Concerns were also mounting about the condition of the current crop. Some floor sources said emergence was slow due to crusting soils. Slow development could lead to a late harvest, they said.
"The remaining supplies to bridge us between old crop and new crop are a lot less than what we anticipated," a pit source said. "That makes the timing of harvest that much more important."
CBOT rice for July delivery closed 15 cents higher at $11.73 per hundredweight.
